topic: Changes in materials exposed to temperature
key_concepts: Matter occupies space and has mass.
Matter has three basic states: solid, liquid, and gas.
Temperature is the degree of hotness or coldness of an object.
Thermometers measure temperature in degrees Celsius or Fahrenheit.
Changes in temperature can cause materials to change phase.
Physical change does not form a new substance and may change shape, size, or phase.
Chemical change forms a new substance and is generally irreversible.
Melting is the change from solid to liquid when heated.
Solidification or freezing is the change from liquid to solid when cooled.
Vaporization is the change from liquid to gas when heated.
Condensation is the change from gas to liquid when cooled.
Burning paper produces ash, a new material that cannot change back into paper.
